title: Suprapubic catheter change
what: A nurse or doctor changes the tube that drains urine from the bladder through the skin above the pubic bone.
why: Regularly, usually every 4 to 6 weeks, or sooner if the tube is blocked or falls out. Your doctor will set the timing.
tell_doctor: When the tube was last changed
If you have a fever, pain, or blood in your urine

prepare.title: Drinking
prepare.text: Drink as usual. A full bladder makes the change easier. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: A normal shower in the morning. Wash the skin around the tube with soap.

steps: The dressing is removed, and the skin around is cleaned with antiseptic
Water is drawn out of the small balloon inside
The old tube is gently removed
A new tube is put into the same opening right away
The balloon is filled, the bag is connected, and a dressing is applied
feel: An unpleasant tugging as the tube comes out
Brief burning as the new one goes in
after: A little blood in the urine in the first hours can happen
Drink more water, unless your doctor has limited it
Write down the date of the next change
red_flags: The tube falls out: call the clinic right away. The opening can close within hours
No urine flows for a few hours, and your belly is swollen
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or redness and pus around the tube

faq.q: Can I change the tube myself?
faq.a: Usually not. A nurse or doctor does it. Some patients are trained. Your doctor decides.

faq.q: What if the tube falls out?
faq.a: Cover the opening with a clean cloth and call the clinic right away. Do not put the tube back yourself.

reminders.text: Suprapubic catheter change tomorrow. Bring a spare bag and your referral.
